name: Ulta Beauty, Inc.
moat_justification: Scale, the broadest mass-plus-prestige assortment in U.S. beauty, and a ~47-million-member loyalty program give Ulta real repeat-purchase and data advantages, but it owns almost no product, switching costs are low, brands can sell through Sephora, Amazon or direct, and pricing is largely set by brands — a narrow retail moat, not a wide one.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 8 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 4.5%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
one_liner: Quality narrow-moat beauty retailer, moat 5/10 — does not clear 15% at $591.36 (weighted IRR 7.72%, weighted IV@15% $232.58); clears 15% only below $232.58.
moat_for: Largest U.S. specialty beauty scale with mass + prestige in one destination
~47M-member loyalty program driving repeat sales and first-party data
Broad assortment as a discovery destination brands need
In-store services and trial that pure e-commerce cannot replicate
Consistently positive owner's earnings (5/5 years) and disciplined buybacks
moat_against: No owned product moat — brands can go direct, to Sephora, or to Amazon
Sephora in Kohl's invading suburban territory with LVMH-backed exclusives
Amazon leading online beauty for replenishment purchases
Low customer switching costs — loyalty points are weak lock-in
U.S. store maturity, consumer pressure, shrink and wage/occupancy costs; Target channel ended
